text: Fill in the missing term in each sentence about β-hCG and prenatal screening.
questions: In normal early pregnancy, β-hCG roughly doubles every *48:How often should the level double in a viable intrauterine pregnancy?* hours; a rise significantly slower than this suggests a failing or ectopic pregnancy.

Above the *discriminatory:What is the name for the β-hCG threshold that triggers ultrasound?* zone, roughly 1500 to 2000 mIU per mL, a transvaginal scan should identify an intrauterine gestational sac.

Prenatal screening markers are reported as multiples of the *median:What statistical measure standardises the marker values?* for gestational age, not as absolute values, so results are comparable across laboratories.

The fourth analyte in the quadruple screen, not present in the triple test, is *inhibin:Which marker was added to AFP, unconjugated oestriol and hCG to form the quadruple test?* A, whose raised level increases the detection rate for Down syndrome.

overallFeedback.feedback: The 48-hour doubling time distinguishes viable from failing pregnancies; the discriminatory zone triggers ultrasound to exclude ectopic pregnancy; multiples of the median standardise screening across laboratories and gestational ages; and inhibin A completes the quadruple test to improve detection of trisomy 21.
